title: Stage representation of sections of an etale sheaf colimit
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and $\Lambda$ a commutative ring. Let $X_{\mathrm{Et}}$ be its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and let $G:\mathcal I\to\mathrm{Mod}(X_{\mathrm{Et}},\Lambda)$ be a diagram of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], indexed by a small filtered category $\mathcal I$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $(H,(c_i))$ be a colimit cocone of $G$. Let $U\to X$ be an object whose underlying scheme is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For every section $t\in H(U)$, there exist an object $i$ of $\mathcal I$ and $s\in G_i(U)$ such that $(c_i)_U(s)=t$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0738 (lemma-directed-colimits-sections), proof of part (4), applied to the etale site as in Etale Cohomology, Tag 03Q4 (section-colimit)

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], identify $H$ with the sheafification of the sectionwise presheaf colimit $P$, respecting the coprojections. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local], $t$ has local representatives in $P$ on an etale covering of $U$.

View the covering as one in the small etale site of $U$: each arrow is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Use [lem-weil-pbc-etale-qcqs-cofinal-finite-coverings] to refine to finitely many affine etale objects $V_b\to U$ with quasi-compact pairwise fibre products. Their composites to $X$ are etale, so they and their overlaps are objects of $X_{\mathrm{Et}}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise], choose a stage representative on each $V_b$. Filteredness places the finitely many representatives at one stage $i$.

On each overlap $V_b\times_U V_{b\prime}$, the difference of the restrictions has zero image in $H$, since both images are restrictions of $t$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-colimit-eventual-zero] on that quasi-compact overlap. Filteredness gives one arrow out of $i$ dominating the finitely many killing arrows, compatibly with each of them (take a cocone over this finite diagram). The transported sections consequently agree on every overlap.

The sheaf equalizer condition [lem-weil-pbc-pretopology-sheaf-condition] glues the transported sections at this stage to a section $s$ over $U$. Its image is $t$ because this equality holds on every member of the covering and $H$ is separated. In the empty-cover case $H(U)$ is zero; filteredness supplies an index and its zero section is a representative.
